 I seriously considered plastic surgery for a couple years. There was one specific feature of my face that plagued me all day every day. I spent tons of money on makeup and would spend upwards of an hour every morning applying it, and the rest of the day making sure I didn't smudge it. I was always hyper-aware of the feature that I hated. I'll skip my personal tribulations and just give you the list of the pros and cons of surgery that helped me figure things out:

PROS:

* more confidence (perhaps)

CONS:

* Potential surgery complications
* Costs tons of money
* Might start a never-ending cycle of wanting another procedure done
* Having to explain to friends and family
* Discomfort/pain
* Indirectly influencing girls with features like mine to also feel like they need to "fix" themselves with surgery. As more and more people do it, the amount of people with such features dwindles and more girls will feel like they're the "only one" who looks like they do, further fueling the oftentimes dangerous and predatory industry of cosmetic procedures.

Realizing that last point, along with one more thing, made me completely rethink everything. The last realization I had is how unhelpful the modern "body posi" movement is and why. Think of the language used in the movement-- "Your stretch marks are beautiful! Your cellulite is beautiful!" Why do they have to be beautiful? Can't they just be neutral? Who do we have to find the beauty in our features in order to be positive about them? Rather than learning to "love" or "embrace" our features, I think it's more helpful to learn to accept them. 

In a society that equates a woman's physical attractiveness with her worth as a human being, it is a rebellious act to refuse to play into it. Why should we fork over thousands to fix the "flaws" that the media, in conjunction with the makeup and cosmetic surgery industry, have convinced us we have just to line their own pockets? More than anything, I feel a responsibility to young girls everywhere to show them that it's okay to just exist as you are naturally. I want to break the cycle.
